anomalies.observed: J17 and J33 are both 8-pin CAN interface connectors; their corresponding pins (including CANH/CANL on pins 4/5) are connected to the same net labels NET0043 and NET0058, making the two connectors electrically identical.
anomalies.expected: The two CAN interfaces should be separate isolated buses, with independent CANH/CANL nets.

evidence.quote: J17 pin 4 -> NET0043; J33 pin 4 -> NET0043; J17 pin 5 -> NET0058; J33 pin 5 -> NET0058
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1) ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B")

anomalies.impact: The two CAN buses are shorted together, eliminating isolation and causing both ODrive controllers to share one bus, leading to communication conflicts.

anomalies.observed: Three MCP2515 CAN controllers (U31, U44, U55) all have their RXCAN and TXCAN pins tied to the same nets NET0028 and NET0133.
anomalies.expected: Each MCP2515 should have its own RXCAN/TXCAN pair connected to a dedicated isolated CAN transceiver; only two controllers are specified.

evidence.quote: U31 pin 2 -> NET0028, pin 3 -> NET0133; U44 pin 2 -> NET0028, pin 3 -> NET0133; U55 pin 2 -> NET0028, pin 3 -> NET0133
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: Multiple CAN controllers drive the same digital CAN signals, causing bus contention and preventing proper independent operation.

anomalies.observed: D9 is a 28V zener in the POE circuit and D10 is an LED; there are no CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diodes on the CAN bus lines.
anomalies.expected: D9 and D10 should be CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays protecting CAN0_P/N and CAN1_P/N.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N
D9 is shown as '28V / 500mW' zener in POE circuit; D10 is 'LED_Dual_KKA' in LED section.

anomalies.impact: CAN buses lack transient/ESD protection, making them vulnerable to damage.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains multiple serious anomalies: the two CAN interface connectors J17 and J33 are wired in parallel, three MCP2515 CAN controllers share the same RXCAN/TXCAN nets, and the specified CAN TVS diodes are missing. These deviations would prevent the board from providing the two independent isolated CAN buses described in the specification.
